newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt yields firm up ahead of repos auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt yields firm up ahead of repos auction.

text.p: Prices of government securities slipped in moderate trade on Monday on apprehensions of a tightening of liquidity, dealers said.
"Market participants were circumspect today as they anticipate a slight tightening of liquidity after the repos auction," a dealer said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) conducts a repos auction later on Monday at which some of the current liquidity is expected to be sucked out of the market.
The funds outflow will take place on Tuesday.
Call money was quoted in the 1.75-2.25 percent range at close of trade on Monday after opening at 2.0-2.50 percent, dealers said.
"The repos auction may be one way of sending a signal to the market that call rates should move up," said a dealer.
"Ideally, call money should be in the five percent to six percent range. The current level is too low," he said.
Yields on government securities rose in subdued trade as most buyers kept off the market, dealers said.
"There was a distinct lack of buying interest today as compared to the last two weeks," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "This led to a price fall."

The 13.50 percent 1998 government of India stock was traded at a yield of 11.18 percent on Monday against the previous yield of 11.14 percent, dealers said. The 12 percent 1999 changed hands at 12.33 percent against 12.28 its last traded price of percent, they added.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper and certificates of deposit.
